teaser: October 2026 is the moment to get into agentic work: companies need AI operators, not model builders, and the edge starts with the application.
core_idea: Agents are moving from pilots to products, and as with breaking apps, building websites or mobile apps before, the skill to run agentic workflows gets people hired now; companies need operators rather than model builders, the data shows employers prefer AI skills, and the edge shows when candidates are equal, starting with an application that brings analysis they have not seen.

quotes.text: Perception changes when people experience it, and only then.

figures.caption: There was a time. Each row is a skill that, for a while, got people hired on what they could show rather than what their CV said: breaking applications, reading code, threat modelling, programming without a degree, building websites, sending email campaigns, building mobile apps after the App Store opened in July 2008, mastering Salesforce or a spreadsheet. Each later became something everyone is expected to know. The last row is now: running agentic workflows.

When all things are equal. Two candidates match the job specification equally well. One sends a CV. The other sends a CV fitted to the role, a short analysis of the company's problem, and an infographic or a small working site they have not seen before. The interview starts from that material, on the candidate's strengths, instead of from gaps in a CV.
